catalog_quote: - la quantité : à la pénultième les voyelles sont toujours prononcée plus ou moins longues. Cette quantité n'a aucune valeur phonologique. d. Tonologie On peut dire qu'elle est normale, mais plus ou moins réversive en ce sens que le "déplacement" ne s'est effectué que sur le préfixe nominal (qui est haut) dans les groupes prépositionnels avec ó ainsi que, parfois, dans le connectif. new_statements.quote: - la quantité : à la pénultième les voyelles sont toujours prononcée plus ou moins longues. Cette quantité n'a aucune valeur phonologique.
new_statements.translation: - quantity: in the penultimate [syllable] the vowels are always pronounced more or less long. This quantity has no phonological value.
new_statements.citation: Motingea Mangulu. 1990. Esquisse du parler des Libobi. In: Parlers riverains de l'entre Ubangi-Zaire. Elements de structure grammaticale (Etudes Aequatoria 8), 68-88. Bamanya: Centre Aequatoria.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (288 pp., byte-identical to the live aequatoria.be asset, HEAD 200 / 43933152 bytes re-checked 2026-09-17T16:26Z). Rendered PDF p.72 (= printed p.69) at 150 dpi and read the page image: under 'Esquisse du parler des Libobi', I. Phonologie, c. Phenomenes vocaliques, the last dash item before 'd. Tonologie' reads exactly '- la quantité : à la pénultième les voyelles sont tou-jours prononcée plus ou moins longues. Cette quanti-té n'a aucune valeur phonologique.' -- verbatim as quoted (only line-break hyphenation differs; the scanned layer has 'pénultiène'). Surrounding section: p.68 gives 7 vowels and the consonant chart; p.69 lists coalescence, elision, progressive vowel harmony, devocal…
new_statements.rule_in_words: In Libobi (a Bamwe variety) the vowel of the penultimate syllable is automatically and non-contrastively lengthened, i.e. a fixed penultimate prominence realised as length; the author does not call it accent or stress, and vowel length is otherwise not phonemic. The language is tonal (two tones H/L, with 'displaced' tonology and a phonetic mid tone).
new_statements.exceptions: None; 'toujours' (always) but 'plus ou moins longues' (more or less long).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain not specified (the statement is in the word-level phonology of the sketch; whether the penult is that of the word or of the phrase/utterance is not said). Stated only in the Libobi sketch (informants from Libulu village, groupement Libobi, zone de Kungu); the Lifonga and Likata sketches of the same 'sous-groupe Bamwe' in the same volume are silent on length and accent, and Donzo 2015 (Libobi, Monyongo) mentions no accent and denies phonological length. Reading 'fixed-penult' is an interpretation of automatic penultimate lengthening as the locus of prominence in a tone language, hence low confidence.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes the Libobi variety (parler des Libóbi: groupement Libobi, zone de Kungu, villages Bolenge, Bosongo, Libulu, Luonga, Boliba; informants from Libulu), which Motingea places in the 'sous-groupe Bamwe' and Glottolog Donzo 2015 likewise counts Libobi speakers among the peoples 'generalement appeles bamwe'. The sister sketches of Lifonga and Likata (same volume) make no corresponding statement, so the penultimate-lengthening remark is attested for Libobi only.

sources.citation: Donzo Bunza Yugia, Jean-Pierre. 2015. Langues bantoues de l'entre Congo-Ubangi (RD Congo): documentation, reconstruction, classification et contacts avec les langues oubanguiennes. PhD thesis, Universite libre de Bruxelles / Universiteit Gent. [Libobi and Monyongo, both 'bamwe', are 2 of the 10 languages described]
sources.note: Nothing on accent/stress. Phonology chapter: seven phonemic vowels; 'La longueur ou quantite vocalique a statut phonologique... est inexistante dans les langues a l'etude' (pp.44-45), only expressive non-distinctive length; two basic tones H/L plus rising/falling contours (p.62). grep accent/penultieme/intensite gives no relevant hit.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu. 1990. Parlers riverains de l'entre Ubangi-Zaire. Elements de structure grammaticale (Etudes Aequatoria 8). Bamanya: Centre Aequatoria. 284 pp. [contains the three Glottolog-listed Bamwe sketches: Le parler des Lifonga pp.32-49, Le parler des Likata pp.49-67, Esquisse du parler des Libobi pp.68-88; open PDF at aequatoria.be]
sources.note: Libobi sketch, I. Phonologie c. Phenomenes vocaliques p.69: vowels of the penultimate syllable are always pronounced more or less long, and this quantity has no phonological value (automatic penultimate lengthening; the word 'accent' is not used). Lifonga phonology pp.32-35 and Likata phonology pp.49-50 treat vowels, consonants and tone ('tonologie deplacee', H/L plus a phonetic mid) and say nothing about accent or length. Whole-volume grep for accent/penulti/intensite/quantite: p.69 is the only prosodic-prominence statement in the book.

sources.note: Tone only: pp.904-906 characterise the 'Bangala-des-marais' (example language: parler de Sombe = Bamwe, terr. Bomboma) as having 'tonologie deplacee' (tone shift one syllable rightward relative to the lingala type); nothing on accent or stress.
